To find the inverse of the matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\), we use the formula for the inverse of a \(2 \times 2\) matrix \(\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}\), which is given by:

\[
\frac{1}{ad - bc} \begin{bmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{bmatrix}
\]

Here, \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\), \(c = 1\), and \(d = 3\).

First, we calculate the determinant:

\[
ad - bc = (2)(3) - (1)(1) = 6 - 1 = 5
\]

Since the determinant is not zero, the matrix is invertible. Now we can find the inverse:

\[
\text{Inverse} = \frac{1}{5} \begin{bmatrix} 3 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{bmatrix}
\]

Final answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} \frac{3}{5} & -\frac{1}{5} \\ -\frac{1}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \end{bmatrix}\)
